rationale: The two-sided acknowledgement check completed. Receipt f0db8b71047e42df96d3e2f4f581835c (exit 0, thirty events, no parse loss) resolves both comparisons: with RestoreCommittedLogs on and the restarted node isolated with one committed voter, both that node and the majority side's own leader acknowledged a client write (comparison 0 violated, witness event index 27, both_sides_acknowledged true), while the flag-off control had no leader on the isolated side so only the majority side acknowledged (comparison 1 holds, evaluated event index 29). That is the strongest witnessed consequence: two leaders partition-side by partition-side each told a client its write succeeded, and one of them rested on two of the committed five voters. FSM divergence and lost acknowledged entries remain unwitnessed and are not claimed. The question now has four complete comparisons with controls; the configuration loss, the minority election and the single-sided acknowledgement are unchanged.

investigations.hypothesis: A node restarted with RestoreCommittedLogs keeps the snapshot's configuration when committed membership changes sit below the restored commit index, so its quorum arithmetic reflects an obsolete membership and it can win an election its committed configuration would forbid.
investigations.discriminator: Grow a snapshot-age three-voter cluster to five voters, restart the leader, compare the configuration index and server count with the log's latest configuration, then isolate the restarted node with one committed voter and check whether it wins with the smaller quorum while the majority side keeps a leader.

knowledge.statement: With Config.RestoreCommittedLogs enabled, a restarted node that keeps a stale smaller configuration can both win leadership on a minority of the committed configuration and acknowledge client writes concurrently with the majority side's own leader: in one execution both sides acknowledged a client write while partitioned, and the flag-off control acknowledged only on the majority side.
knowledge.conditions: Committed configuration grown from three to five voters after the restarting node's snapshot; RestoreCommittedLogs=true with a CommitTrackingLogStore; the node isolated together with one committed voter immediately after NewRaft returns, that partner also cut off from the majority side; a bounded wait for the majority side to hold its own leader before either write; two second apply timeout and two second heal settle.

gaps.question: Does a leader elected with fewer votes than the committed configuration requires reproduce reliably, under which schedule and partition order, and does the committed configuration's majority side then diverge in committed entries?

interpretations.rationale: Four completed comparisons, each with its flag-off control in the same execution, answer this question. Configuration: receipt b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826, comparison 0 violated at witness event index 15 - the node restarted from a log whose latest configuration is index 14 with five servers came back at configuration index 1 with three servers - control holding at evaluated event index 18 (index 14, five servers). Election: receipt abfdbd1823b342409ef4a815bade0407, comparison 0 violated at witness event index 22 - isolated with one committed voter immediately after NewRaft returned, the node became leader with reachable_votes 2 against committed_quorum 3, with majority_side_leader also true - control holding at evaluated event index 25. Single-side acknowledgement: receipt 568bebb18e574cafa18e96add68e89db, comparison 0 violated at witness event index 27 - the isolated leader's Apply completed (minority_apply_ok true) - control holding at evaluated event index 29. Two-sided acknowledgement: receipt f0db8b71047e42df96d3e2f4f581835c, comparison 0 violated at witness event index 27 - with a bounded wait for the majority side to hold its own leader, both it and the isolated node acknowledged a client write - control holding at evaluated event index 29, where only the majority side acknowledged. Source: restoreFromCommittedLogs (api.go:724-754) advances lastApplied to the persisted commit index before the startup scan at api.go:604-620, so AddVoter's later entry (api.go:994-1005) is never re-read and the node keeps the snapshot's three-server list; quorumSize() (raft.go:1087-1094) then returns two, electSelf (raft.go:1999-2060) asks only that list, and the commitment calculation (commitment.go:78-104) accepts two matching indexes as a quorum, so leadership and acknowledgements rest on a majority of an obsolete configuration rather than of the committed one. The manoeuvre the runs needed - also cutting the single committed voter off from the majority side so requestVote's existing-leader guard (raft.go:1690-1700) does not refuse the vote - is an ordinary partition shape; the minority leadership appeared in the immediate-isolation executions and not in the settled-schedule ones, so the manifestation is schedule dependent while the decisions and acknowledgements are unrepaired by the library.
counterevidence: The flag-off controls in all four receipts keep the committed configuration, cannot win on the isolated side and do not acknowledge there.
Two settled-schedule executions did not produce the minority leadership, explained by whether the isolated partner still heard the majority-side leader; no frequency or absence claim is made.
FSM divergence and lost acknowledged entries did not appear: the applied-slice comparison at the conflict index did not line up and no entry was recovered after healing.
limitations: Every observation is bounded (three second majority-leader wait, five second election window, two second apply timeout, two second heal settle), so no occurrence-rate or absence bound is established.
No entry-level divergence or lost acknowledged entry is witnessed; the probe only shows that both sides answered the client.
The scenario restarts the former leader of a cluster grown by adding voters; other roles, change types, chain orders and durable stores are not explored.

7da03e78394f41fdad540ae0824ec2a6-gap-1.explanation: Election and acknowledgement are resolved by complete comparisons with controls: abfdbd1823b342409ef4a815bade0407 (witness index 22, control 25), 568bebb18e574cafa18e96add68e89db (witness 27, control 29) and f0db8b71047e42df96d3e2f4f581835c (witness 27, control 29), the last showing both sides acknowledging a client write concurrently. Reproduction depends on whether the single committed voter on the isolated side still hears the majority-side leader, because requestVote refuses candidates while a leader is known (raft.go:1690-1700): with immediate isolation it reproduced in every execution, with the settled schedule it did not. Entry-level divergence still has no witness, so that part of the gap stays open.

interpretations.joint_history: Four complete executions of the same five-voter scenario over identical stores, sizes and snapshot timing supply the four comparisons: b15f4b6c55b44402ace926204de9b826 (configuration loss and control), abfdbd1823b342409ef4a815bade0407 (election and control), 568bebb18e574cafa18e96add68e89db (single-side acknowledgement and control) and f0db8b71047e42df96d3e2f4f581835c (two-sided acknowledgement and control). Each receipt built its own cluster and stores and is a complete history in itself; only the comparison declarations, the bounded majority-leader wait and the result event names differ between them, and the configuration values agree across all four (flagged side at index 1 with three servers against expected 14 with five; controls at 14 with five), so none is a fragment of another.
